day_shape: 74 items: Bessent declares 'economic D-Day' against Iran in FT op-ed, CENTCOM reports 70 vessels redirected under Hormuz blockade, Oman FM travelling to Tehran, Iran SNSC chief Rezaee threatens total oil halt, rial hits 2m/$.

threads.label: Hormuz blockade and shipping enforcement
threads.summary: CENTCOM said US forces have redirected 70 commercial vessels, disabled 3 and boarded 2 enforcing the blockade against Iran, while Jerusalem Post reported traffic remained below average. Iran's Persian Gulf waterway body warned non-compliant vessels face fines, detention or confiscation, and Defa Press disputed Barak Ravid's tanker transit figures citing Kpler data of 7 ships.

threads.label: US economic war and Iran response
threads.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent wrote in the FT that 'economic D-Day' against Iran 'begins at dawn', with Jerusalem Post citing experts on further options including sanctions on Chinese teapot refineries. SNSC head Mohsen Rezaee told IRIB Iran has made billions despite sanctions and warned that if the economic war continues, 'not a drop of oil' will exit the Strait of Hormuz.

threads.label: Regional diplomacy around Tehran
threads.summary: Iran's foreign ministry announced Oman FM Badr Al Busaidi will visit Tehran Tuesday to continue talks on the Strait of Hormuz, and that Pakistan army chief Asim Munir will also travel to Tehran. Jerusalem Post reported Pakistan positioning as a potential Tehran-Washington mediator and Iran being invited to the Saudi-Turkey-Pakistan Mecca Agreement for Mutual Defense.

threads.label: Gaza strikes and kite escalation
threads.summary: IDF said it killed Hamas weapons-production commander Ismail Abu Ful in Maghazi and a Nukhba platoon commander in Khan Younis, while Netanyahu and Katz warned strikes would intensify against those launching kites from Gaza after four landed in Kibbutz Nahal Oz. Palestinian media reported casualties from strikes near az-Zawayda and Khan Younis.

threads.label: Iran threats and nuclear doctrine signals
threads.summary: Iran International reported the SNSC's top security official hinted Tehran could reconsider its rejection of nuclear weapons after US strikes, and that Iranian state TV aired a segment referencing a $10 million reward tied to Barron Trump. Jerusalem Post cited claims Iranian hackers shut down a British power plant for four days in July, and that Greece moved a Patriot battery to protect a base.

threads.label: Lebanon and Syria fronts
threads.summary: Jerusalem Post reported the IDF is accelerating destruction of Hezbollah infrastructure in southern Lebanon on Katz's orders, and IRIB reported fresh Israeli artillery strikes on Hula and Mansouri. The World Bank projected Lebanon's economy to shrink 6.4% in 2026, while Syria said it expects security-deal negotiations with Israel to resume.

threads.label: Iran domestic pressure and executions
threads.summary: Iran International reported the rial hit a historic 2 million to the dollar with Iranians describing deepening hardship, and that another January-protest detainee was executed after the Supreme Court upheld his sentence. Defa Press reported an IRGC-police 'strategic synergy' conference in Tehran on internal security coordination, while Khamenei's office issued a message urging combat against 'despair, fear and suspicion'.

events.title_en: Oman's foreign minister travelling to Tehran
events.summary_en: Oman's foreign minister travelling to Tehran. The Foreign Ministry spokesperson announced to reporters that Seyyed Badr Al Busaidi, Oman's Minister of Foreign Affairs, is travelling to Tehran. Al Busaidi's visit is scheduled for Tuesday, 3 Shahrivar, during which Oman's foreign minister will meet with Seyyed Abbas Araghchi, Iran's Minister of Foreign Affairs, to discuss bilateral and regional matters. This visit is in line with strengthening bilateral Iran-Oman cooperation and continuing ongoing political consultations between the two countries as two littoral states of the Strait of Hormuz, in order to help strengthen peace and security in the region.

Across the world, particularly in developed countries, citizens benefit from special services commensurate with their circumstances and characteristics, and some of these services are made available to them in the form of discounts or free of charge. Currently, metro and bus services remain free until the end of the imposed war with America.

events.summary_en: Waste landslide in Guinea with at least 30 dead. A massive waste slide at Conakry's largest landfill, capital of Guinea, left at least 30 dead and 22 injured. The incident occurred Sunday morning following heavy rainfall and buried surrounding houses under heaps of waste. Search and rescue operations continue with the presence of emergency and army forces, and local authorities have warned of a possible rise in the death toll.

events.summary_en: Trump has no option against Iran, says Stephen Walt, US international relations professor. Trump has no option against Iran and speaks nonsense. The US President's claim to declare the Strait of Hormuz as a potential new American domain is ridiculous and shows he has lost his options. Iran both controls the Strait of Hormuz and enforces law in the Persian Gulf. A war by America against Iran has never had the support of the American people and before it began, the majority of Americans would not have supported it. Iranians have no reason to believe anything Trump tells them or any promise or commitment he makes in exchange for concessions. So they only wait...

events.title: A Hamas terrorist who invaded Israel during the October 7, 2023, onslaught was targeted in an Israeli strike in the southern Gaza Strip yesterday, the military says. The strike in Khan Younis targeted a company commander in Hamas's elite Nukhba Force, according to the IDF. He is not named, and his condition is unclear. Palestinian media reported that the strike wounded several people. In addition to invading Israel on October 7, the IDF says that the Hamas terrorist has advanced attacks on troops in the Strip. "The terrorist's activities posed an immediate threat to our forces," the military says, justifying the strike amid the ceasefire.

events.title_en: Zionist reporter Barak Ravid's lie about ship transit through the Strait of Hormuz
events.summary_en: Zionist reporter Barak Ravid's lie about ship transit through the Strait of Hormuz. Whilst Barak Ravid, reporter for Zionist website Axios, claims that 40 tankers transited the Strait of Hormuz by last Friday and carried 16 million barrels of oil, open-source tracking data refutes this claim. Tracking firm Kpler announced that only 7 ships transited the Strait of Hormuz last Thursday. Furthermore, 16 million barrels would require several supertankers, which with the recent observable transit of single-digit numbers of vessels would be difficult to reconcile with this claim. America claims that protected convoys transit at night and their tracking systems are switched off.
